newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY'S GHEDINA FASTEST IN DOWNHILL TRAINING.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY'S GHEDINA FASTEST IN DOWNHILL TRAINING.

text.p: Italy's Kristian Ghedina was fastest in men's downhill training at the world Alpine skiing championships on Thursday but the times meant little with many top racers either competing in the combined event or saving their energy.
France's Luc Alphand, a favourite for the gold in the discipline, stayed in his hotel. Team officials said he was still taking antibiotics for a cold although he was much better.
Norway's Atle Skaardal, winner of Monday's opening super-G and unrelated Austrians Fritz and Josef Strobl were also nowhere to be seen.
That left Ghedina, winner of three World Cup downhills this season, to clock the fastest time of one minute 37.83 seconds but he said later little could be read into it.
The Kandahar piste had been made rough and uneven by 57 combined skiers going down it earlier on a bright, sunny day.
"The piste was really ruined," he said. "Yesterday it was much faster. There's a big hole. But it was an important test because I had a few things to sort out."
The men's downhill is on Saturday with the final training session scheduled for Friday.
